claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-week Phase 1/2 trial in 94 people with MASLD (BMI >=28.0 kg/m^2, liver fat >=10% by imaging), once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide produced dose-dependent reductions in liver fat content (46.6% at 1.2 mg, 68.5% at 1.8 mg, 57.1% at 2.4 mg vs 4.4% for placebo) and body-weight loss peaking at -4.3% at the 1.8 mg dose (p<0.001), and was reported as well tolerated with no severe or serious adverse events.

claims.statement: In the Phase 2b IMPACT trial (212 participants with biopsy-confirmed MASH, fibrosis stages F2/F3), 24-week once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide produced MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis in 59.1% (1.2 mg) and 52.1% (1.8 mg) of participants versus 19.1% for placebo (p<.0001 both doses); fibrosis improvement without worsening MASH occurred in 31.8% and 34.5% of the 1.2 mg and 1.8 mg groups respectively versus 25.9% for placebo, a difference reported as not statistically significant; mean weight loss was 5.0% (1.2 mg) and 6.2% (1.8 mg) versus 1.0% for placebo (p<.001).

claims.statement: According to Altimmune's sponsor-reported topline results for the 48-week Phase 2 MOMENTUM obesity trial (n=391), gastrointestinal adverse events at the highest dose (2.4 mg weekly) included nausea in 51.5%, vomiting in 27.8%, diarrhea in 18.6%, and constipation in 22.7% of participants, described as mostly mild-to-moderate; drug-related discontinuation rates were reported as 15.5% (2.4 mg) and 16.2% (1.8 mg) versus 2.1% for placebo, and one serious vomiting event was reported at the 2.4 mg dose. An independent trade-wire outlet (TipRanks/The Fly) independently reports matching drug-related discontinuation rates (4.1%/16.2%/15.5% at 1.2/1.8/2.4 mg vs 2.1% placebo) and independently characterizes GI adverse events as predominantly mild-to-moderate nausea and vomiting; the exact per-symptom percentages (51.5% nausea, 27.8% vomiting, 18.6% diarrhea, 22.7% constipation) and the one serious vomiting event remain sourced only to the sponsor and have not been independently reproduced.

conflicts.summary: MASH-resolution endpoint reached strong statistical significance in the IMPACT Phase 2b trial, but the co-primary/secondary fibrosis-improvement endpoint did not separate significantly from placebo at 24 weeks, which trade-press coverage of the topline data does not consistently emphasize alongside the MASH-resolution headline figures. Resolved 2026-08-29: the peer-reviewed Lancet publication (PMID 41237796) independently confirms both the MASH-resolution figures and the non-significant fibrosis-improvement result, matching the packet's existing caveat.

The MOMENTUM 48-week obesity trial's efficacy and safety figures were initially available only via sponsor (Altimmune) topline press release; remediation-pass-2026-08-29's first attempt (ClinicalTrials.gov API, Europe PMC, ADA conference abstract) found no independent source. Resolved 2026-08-29 (remediation update, per independent-review verdict): independent trade-press coverage now corroborates the core figures -- TipRanks/The Fly independently reports matching drug-related discontinuation rates and GI-tolerability characterization for the safety claim, and Patient Care Online (with Clinical Trials Arena/ADA 2024 coverage) independently reproduces the weight-loss-by-dose and 32.1% >=20%-responder figures for the efficacy claim. A residual subset of figures (exact per-symptom AE percentages, the single serious vomiting event, and the 71.4% >=10%-responder figure) remains sponsor-sourced only and is documented as such in each claim's reviewFlags.
